newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate drops to 5.5 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate drops to 5.5 pct in Jan.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate dipped to 5.5 percent in January from 6.1 percent in December, the state Employment Security Commission said Wednesday.
The commission revised the December rate, which it previously said had dropped to 5.6 percent, down from 6.2 percent in November.

The total of nonfarm jobs dropped by 39,700 in January, but the jobless rate also declined because many temporary workers who lost jobs in January also dropped out of the work force, commission analyst Sam McClary said.
The largest decreases were in trade, which lost 16,100 jobs and in services, which lost 10,700 jobs, largely due to seasonal declines in the retail and tourism industries.

Government jobs were down by 7,500, partly because many schools still were on holiday break. Manufacturing lost 1,700 jobs, including 600 in textiles. Construction lost 1,700 jobs, while finance, insurance and real estate lost 800 jobs.
Williamsburg County had the highest jobles rate, 19.8 percent, and Lexington County had the lowest, 2.8 percent.
